correctness.rationale: For every prime \(q\in(c/2,c]\), Legendre's formula gives \(v_q(c!)=1\), so \(q\mid s(c!)\). Exact enumeration handles \(1\le c\le50\). For \(c\ge51\), two applications of Nagura's theorem to \(c/2\) and \(5c/6\) produce distinct primes in disjoint subintervals of \((c/2,c]\), proving non-primality. The verifier independently reproduces all finite computations.

value.rationale: The classification is attached to the central parameter set \(\mathcal{S}\) in a 2026 theorem on products of factorials and identifies its complete atomic one-prime-support layer. It gives an exact global threshold \(c=11\) beyond which at least two primes are forced into every squarefree kernel. This is a natural complete classification, not a recomputation of a finite table.
